_comment: Scored-episode rosters and leaderboard wiring for the V2D Challenge.
Editing this file is the supported way to change which episodes are scored, the
Public/Private split, the metric set, or the Kaggle competition slugs.
family=object_pose: the participant submits the rolled-out object trajectory and the host
recomputes every metric. Definition of record is flash_chord/evaluation/metrics.py.
Track 2: the organizer confirmed that all three tiers score against the same clean multi-view reference; tier inputs differ.
worlds_per_episode: how many parallel evaluation worlds the submitted trajectory carries.
evaluate_policy.py defaults to world_count=4096, but under reset_mode=explicit every world
resets to the same frame and runs a deterministic policy, so the cohort is expected to be
redundant and only one world is submitted. Raise this if that turns out to be wrong; the
schema already carries a world_index and needs no code change.
accepted_eval_script_sha256 / accepted_eval_code_sha256: allowlists of released evaluator
digests. The script hash covers evaluate_policy.py and is stable; the code hash covers the
evaluation modules and is what changes when the scoring maths changes. A submission
reporting anything else is rejected. An empty list disables that check. Adding a hash needs
a new metric-notebook version AND re-selecting it on each competition, and does NOT rescore
existing submissions, so only ever append.
private_fraction is 0: every scored row appears on Kaggle's Public leaderboard. Reference data may still be confidential, depending on the track.

track_2_tier1.title: Track 2 - Robotic Grounding (Tier 1: multi-view input)
track_2_tier1.input_note: Use the original SOMA-X human and object reconstruction in the released Tier 1 multiview-caption dataset. This is the clean trajectory used as the configured scoring reference.

track_2_tier2.title: Track 2 - Robotic Grounding (Tier 2: synthetically corrupted input)
track_2_tier2.input_note: Use the released Tier 2 synthetic-noise trajectories. Human and object poses are perturbed while episode timing, videos, visibility, identity parameters, and meshes are preserved. The configured scoring reference is the clean Tier 1 object trajectory.

track_2_tier3.title: Track 2 - Robotic Grounding (Tier 3: bring your own reconstruction)
track_2_tier3.input_note: No trajectory is supplied. Reconstruct the sequences yourself from the videos, by whatever method you prefer, and drive your policy from that. The tier is method-agnostic on purpose: the reconstruction is part of what you are being judged on, and you are scored against the clean multi-view trajectory regardless of how you got there.

track_3.title: Track 3 - Egocentric
track_3.scored_episodes_note: The 20 holdout episodes whose egocentric videos are released in track_3/evaluation. The holdout's other 5 (4, 7, 9, 17, 34) have ground truth but no released video, so they cannot be scored.

track_3_mesh.title: Track 3 - Egocentric (object reconstruction)
track_3_mesh.leaderboard_group_note: Its own Kaggle competition, because a mesh per (episode, object) has nothing in common with the per-frame pose rows the other Track 3 metrics score; the aggregator shows it as a column of the Track 3 table.

timeline.submission_limit: five times per week, with unlimited submissions during the final three days
timeline._comment: The official challenge site currently states November 4, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. EST. Align each Kaggle competition deadline before launch.

_comment: Fields for the competition-specific half of the Kaggle rules. Anything left null is
rendered as a loud NEEDS DECISION marker rather than guessed, because these are legal
terms and a plausible-looking wrong one is worse than an obvious gap.
Disagreements between this, the challenge website and the live Kaggle settings are
resolved in favour of the WEBSITE, because that is what participants read before they
enter. Where the website promises something Kaggle cannot express, the rules state the
website's policy and note the mechanism; see submission_policy.
max_team_size and max_daily_submissions are what the competition is CONFIGURED with, and
tools/verify_competitions.py errors if a live competition differs. Neither is settable
through the API, so both are set by hand in the Kaggle UI.
